NKE.rationale: NKE is in a severe fundamental deterioration with no credible near-term re-rating catalyst. The company's earnings trajectory is sharply negative: Q3 FY2026 EPS of $0.35 represents a -35.2% YoY decline and -34.0% QoQ decline, with operating income collapsing to $650M from $844M a year ago. Revenue is essentially flat YoY (+0.1%) but margins are compressing rapidly—gross margin fell to 40.1% in Q3 from 41.4% a year ago, and operating margin collapsed to 5.8% from 7.5%. Operating cash flow has deteriorated dramatically to $430M in Q3 from $1.79B in the year-ago quarter, a -76% YoY decline. The balance sheet shows total liabilities of $22.97B against equity of $14.09B, with leverage increasing. Valuation remains expensive despite the selloff: at $42.29, the stock trades at 27.8x trailing P/E with only 4.8% net margin and 16% ROE—both well below historical norms (net margin was 9.4% and ROE was 32.2% just a year ago). The P/E has compressed from 38.9x in January 2026 but remains elevated given the earnings trajectory. The stock has fallen 47% from its 52-week high of $80.17, yet the fundamental picture continues to worsen. Greater China revenues declined 12% reported and 17% currency-neutral in Q4, with six consecutive quarters of decline. Management guidance for FY2027 calls for low-to-mid single-digit revenue declines in Q1 and further deceleration in Q2. Tariff headwinds of 10-15% on Vietnam, Indonesia, and China supply chains add ~$1.5B in annual costs. The 'Win Now' turnaround strategy is in early stages with no evidence of sustainable improvement. News sentiment is negative (mean -0.141 over 90 days). The next earnings event (Sep 24, 2026) is more likely to be a downside catalyst given the weak guidance trajectory. All three pillars—deteriorating fundamentals, still-elevated valuation, and negative near-term catalysts—align bearishly.
